q:
Cloze Test (1/5): Select the most appropriate option for Blank No. 1.

'The rapid growth of technology has (1)______ our lives in many ways. It has (2)______ communication easier and faster. However, over-dependence on gadgets (3)______ lead to health issues. We must find a (4)______ between screen time and physical activities. Adopting a mindful (5)______ is the need of the hour.'
e: Blank 1: 'Transformed' fits best as technology has changed our lives significantly.

q:
Cloze Test (2/5): Select the most appropriate option for Blank No. 2.

'The rapid growth of technology has (1)______ our lives. It has (2)______ communication easier and faster. However, gadgets (3)______ lead to health issues...'
e: Blank 2: 'Has' ke sath V3 (made) ka prayog hota hai (Present Perfect).

q:
Cloze Test (3/5): Select the most appropriate option for Blank No. 3.

'...communication easier and faster. However, over-dependence on gadgets (3)______ lead to health issues. We must find a (4)______...'
e: Blank 3: 'Can' yahan possibility (sambhvana) ko darshata hai.

q:
Cloze Test (4/5): Select the most appropriate option for Blank No. 4.

'...over-dependence leads to health issues. We must find a (4)______ between screen time and physical activities. Adopting a mindful (5)______...'
e: Blank 4: Screen time aur physical activity ke beech 'Balance' banaya jata hai.

q:
Cloze Test (5/5): Select the most appropriate option for Blank No. 5.

'...We must find a balance. Adopting a mindful (5)______ is the need of the hour.'
e: Blank 5: 'Mindful approach' (sachet nazariya) ek standard phrase hai.

q: Error Spotting: No sooner had (A) / the news appeared in the scroll (B) / when there was (C) / a huge rush at the counter (D).
e: Rule: 'No sooner' ka pair hamesha 'than' hota hai, 'when' nahi.

q: Error Spotting: The population of Mumbai (A) / is greater (B) / than (C) / Delhi (D).
e: Rule: Comparison 'than that of Delhi' hona chahiye kyunki hum cities nahi, population compare kar rahe hain.

q: Error Spotting: If I would have (A) / worked hard (B) / I would have (C) / passed the exam (D).
e: Conditional: 'If' clause mein 'had + V3' lagta hai, 'would have' nahi.

q: Error Spotting: Scarcely had I (A) / finished the typing (B) / than the manager (C) / called me (D).
e: Pairing: Scarcely/Hardly ke sath 'when' lagta hai.

q: Error Spotting: The news (A) / are (B) / broadcasted (C) / daily (D).
e: Rule: 'News' singular hai, isliye 'is' lagega. Broadcast ki teeno forms 'broadcast' hi rehti hain.

q: Sentence Improvement: He is *senior than* me in the office.
e: Senior/Junior/Superior ke sath 'to' lagta hai.

q: Sentence Improvement: If I *was* a king, I would help the poor.
e: Imagination ke liye 'were' ka prayog hota hai.

q: Sentence Improvement: She *denied to help* me in the project.
e: Request mana karne ke liye 'refuse' aur facts ke liye 'deny' lagta hai.

q: Sentence Improvement: Bread and butter *are* my favorite breakfast.
e: Bread-butter ek single unit hai, isliye singular 'is' lagega.

q: Sentence Improvement: The manager requested the staff to *keep off* the unnecessary expenses.
e: Keep down matlab control/kharch kam karna.

q: Synonym of 'ABUNDANT':
e: Abundant matlab prachur/bahut zyada.

q: Antonym of 'FRUGAL':
e: Frugal matlab kanjoos, Extravagant matlab fuzool-kharch.

q: One-word Substitution: A person who believes that pleasure is the most important thing.
e: Hedonist wo hota hai jo sirf sharirik sukh ko mahatva deta hai.

q: One-word Substitution: One who knows many languages.
e: Bahut bhashayein janne wale ko Polyglot kehte hain.

q: Idiom: 'At the eleventh hour' means:
e: Iska matlab hota hai ekdam antim samay par.

q: Idiom: 'A piece of cake' means:
e: Iska matlab hota hai bahut hi asaan kaam.

q: Active/Passive: The police arrested the thief.
o: The thief was arrested by police
e: Past Simple hamesha 'was + V3' mein badalta hai.

q: Active/Passive: Who can count the stars?
o: By whom can the stars be counted?
Can stars be counted by whom?
e: 'Who' badal kar 'By whom' aur modal + be + V3 lagta hai.

q: Active/Passive: Close the door.
e: Imperative sentences 'Let + Object + be + V3' se bante hain.

q: Direct/Indirect: He said, 'I am busy'.
o: He said that he was busy
e: Present 'am' badal kar Past 'was' ho jata hai.

q: Direct/Indirect: She said, 'Please help me'.
o: She told me to help her
She requested me to help her
e: 'Please' badal kar 'Requested' ho jata hai.

q: Direct/Indirect: The teacher said, 'The Earth is round'.
e: Universal Truth ka tense kabhi nahi badalta.

q: Sentence Rearrangement: P: football Q: they R: playing S: are
e: Correct: They are playing football (QSRP).

q: Sentence Rearrangement: P: Bihar Q: is R: state S: a big
e: Correct: Bihar is a big state (PQSR).

q: Synonym of 'CANDID':
e: Candid matlab jo saaf-saaf bole (Frank).

q: Antonym of 'HAUGHTY':
e: Haughty matlab ghamandi, Humble matlab vinamra.

q: Select correctly spelt word:
e: Sahi spelling 'Occurrence' hai.

q: Select correctly spelt word:
e: Sahi spelling 'Meticulous' hai.

q: Cloze (Misc): I am looking forward to ________ you.
e: 'Looking forward to' ke baad Gerund (V1+ing) lagta hai.

q: Cloze (Misc): The sun __________ in the east.
e: Universal truth: Present Simple (V1+s).
